macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. equity futures rise ahead of Anthropic IPO debut
items.summary: U.S. stock futures climbed Thursday, with Nasdaq 100 futures up 2.3%, S&P 500 futures up 1.2% and Dow futures up 0.7%, as investors anticipated Anthropic’s market debut.[1]

items.title: Fed minutes signal further rate increases
items.summary: Minutes from the Federal Reserve’s October meeting showed that almost all policymakers supported additional rate increases to contain inflation. Markets were pricing in a near-certain 25-basis-point hike at the December meeting.[7]

items.title: Wall Street closes mixed after hawkish Fed signals
items.summary: The Dow fell 1.11% to 50,198.17, the S&P 500 declined 0.23% to 7,323.64, and the Nasdaq rose 0.42% to 24,429.89 on Wednesday as investors weighed Fed minutes and Nvidia’s results.[7]

items.title: Anthropic prices IPO above initial range
items.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above the top of its initial range, in what was described as one of the largest stock-market IPOs and the first major listing by a frontier AI model developer.[7]

items.title: U.S. jobless claims rise; Philadelphia Fed manufacturing weakens
items.summary: Initial jobless claims increased to 203,000 for the week ended November 14, while the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index fell to 6.3 in November from 20.9 in October.[2]

items.title: Palo Alto Networks raises guidance and announces acquisition
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks shares rose after the cybersecurity company reported better-than-expected quarterly results, raised full-year guidance and agreed to acquire Applied Compute for $4.5 billion.[6]

items.title: Nvidia shares fall despite earnings beat
items.summary: Nvidia reported quarterly results and guidance above analyst expectations, but its shares fell 2.9% amid investor uncertainty following co-founder Jensen Huang’s reported departure.[7]

items.title: Asian markets diverge
items.summary: Japan’s Nikkei closed 0.7% higher, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 2% and China’s Shanghai Composite declined 0.3%.[2]

items.title: Palo Alto, Intel and Tesla shares gain in premarket trading
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks rose 8.6% after its results and guidance update, Intel gained 3.9% after reporting an external customer for its advanced 18A chips, and Tesla advanced 1.6% following reports of increased Shanghai production.[2]

items.title: Walmart, Alibaba and NetEase shares decline after earnings
items.summary: Walmart and Alibaba fell 1.5% and 1.9%, respectively, after quarterly reports, while NetEase dropped 5.6% after reporting lower third-quarter non-GAAP net income and revenue.[2]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ether slide amid rate fears and liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin fell to about $63,874, down 1.69% in 24 hours and more than 13% over seven days, while Ether dropped 1.89% to roughly $1,790. A leveraged liquidation wave erased approximately $2 billion in positions, concentrated among long traders.

items.title: Coinbase expands on-chain lending to New York
items.summary: Coinbase’s crypto-backed lending product is now available to New York residents after approval from the New York State Department of Financial Services. The service uses Morpho infrastructure on Base and allows eligible users to borrow USDC against crypto collateral.

items.title: Polymarket adopts Chainlink pricing for crypto markets
items.summary: Polymarket International switched hourly and daily cryptocurrency prediction markets from Binance reference prices to Chainlink Data Streams, using a 60-second USD-denominated time-weighted average price.

items.title: BlackRock-linked wallet transfers $315 million in BTC and ETH
items.summary: A wallet associated with BlackRock’s ETF transferred approximately 4,482 BTC and 15,380 ETH, together worth about $315 million, to Coinbase Prime across four transactions.

items.title: CFTC approval sends Backpack token sharply higher
items.summary: Backpack’s BP token gained about 30% in 24 hours to approximately $1.10 after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission approved two regulatory applications for the exchange’s U.S. derivatives operations.

items.title: ASIC shuts down more than 20 crypto-related websites
items.summary: Australia’s Securities and Investments Commission reportedly shut down more than 20 websites linked to QUFC Exchange and issued a consumer warning about the platform.

items.title: Russia plans regulated crypto access for qualified investors
items.summary: Russia’s central bank plans to amend legislation in 2027 to permit investment funds to buy cryptocurrencies for qualified investors, while introducing investor testing before broader crypto-market access.

items.title: World Bank studies stablecoin-based cross-border payments
items.summary: The World Bank is working with Circle and Citigroup to explore whether stablecoins can improve the traceability and efficiency of cross-border payments into developing economies. The initiative remains exploratory and has not launched a payment service.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Microsoft and OpenAI announce new AI models
items.summary: Microsoft introduced seven MAI models at Ignite, including systems for coding, cybersecurity, image generation, speech, transcription, and decision-making. OpenAI reportedly released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, positioned for complex and everyday tasks respectively.

items.title: Microsoft Decision 1.1 becomes generally available
items.summary: Microsoft announced general availability of Microsoft-Decision-1.1, a lower-cost, low-latency model designed to make software decisions dynamically at scale. It is available through Microsoft Foundry and selected partner platforms.

items.title: Microsoft Maia 200 AI accelerator enters production
items.summary: Microsoft said its Maia 200 AI accelerator is now in production, with the chip designed to run large models while improving energy efficiency. The announcement reflects growing competition over AI infrastructure, operating costs, and performance per watt.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly prepares for major IPO
items.summary: Anthropic is reportedly planning to become a public company, potentially in one of the largest technology IPOs. The development comes amid intensified competition among Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google over frontier models and enterprise AI.

items.title: AI industry competition shifts toward efficiency and enterprise deployment
items.summary: Recent launches emphasize specialized models, lower inference costs, energy efficiency, cybersecurity, coding, and integration into business software rather than only benchmark performance. Microsoft’s multi-model release illustrates the broader trend toward task-specific AI systems.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches worldwide
items.summary: Rockstar Games’ long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI has begun rolling out worldwide for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, returning players to Vice City after a 13-year wait.[3]

items.title: Gaming consoles see surge ahead of GTA VI release
items.summary: UK retailers reported sharply higher demand for consoles and gaming accessories ahead of GTA VI’s launch, while some employers and organizations introduced special leave or other accommodations for players.[5]

items.title: Esports Nations Cup 2027 qualification expands
items.summary: The Esports Foundation expanded the road to the 2027 Esports Nations Cup with national-team events, additional qualification tournaments, larger rosters and a new ranking system.[1]

items.title: World of Dokkaebi tops mobile-game revenue charts in Korea
items.summary: Kakao Games’ 2.5D MMORPG The World of Dokkaebi reportedly reached the top revenue position on both Google Play and Apple’s App Store in Korea on November 18, the same day it received an Excellence Award at the 2026 Korea Game Awards.[9]

items.title: GameRecruit launches German corporate esports league
items.summary: GameRecruit announced a new corporate esports league in Germany, with separate northern and southern competitions and 24 available team places.[1]
